content: The dosing of kola nut (Cola nitida) is specific to its indication, but no standard dosage has been established, as it varies depending on its use in commercial beverages. It is possibly effective in managing physical and mental fatigue, though evidence remains limited. Fluconazole has been shown to increase the levels of kola nut in the body by reducing its metabolism. Similarly, grapefruit can also elevate kola nut levels through the same mechanism. However, the clinical significance of these interactions is considered minor and remains unclear. Adverse effects associated with kola nut include tachycardia (increased heart rate). There is no established pregnancy category or lactation safety data for kola nut. However, it is generally considered acceptable for use during pregnancy, as controlled studies in pregnant women have not demonstrated any evidence of fetal risk.
